summary: An element whose content item is a whole form XObject, named by an /OBJR and found through the form's own /StructParent (14.7.5.4's EXAMPLE 1), gets none of the form's text. by_absence builds the ranges included in the structure tree from MCID sequences, declared artifacts and annotations claimed by /StructParent, so the form's text is reported as an artifact by absence; Tree::logical_text reads only MarkedContent children, so the logical text omits it; and viewer-core's walk records an /OBJR only through names_object, which matches the page's annotations, so the element's accessibility node has an empty name. The same form drawn inside the element's own MCID sequence is real content on all three routes.
source: ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.3: "When a structure element's content consists of an entire PDF object, such as an XObject directly or indirectly referenced by a page description or an annotation, the object shall be identified in the structure element's K entry by an object reference dictionary". §14.8.2.2.2: "Any content that is not included in the structure tree is an artifact even when not enclosed in a markedcontent sequence using the tag Artifact ." §14.7.5.4: "For consistency, content items that are entire PDF objects, such as XObjects, shall also use the parent tree to refer to their parent structure elements."

summary: A structured marked-content sequence nested in a Span that states /Lang takes the Span's language when no structure element above it states one, instead of the document's default. ContentStream::accessibility sets the sequence's language to structure::enclosing's, which is None when no ancestor element has /Lang, and accessibility::speech then lets the enclosing Span's Described cover it. Where an ancestor element states a language it wins correctly; only the inheritance that ends at the catalog loses to the Span.
source: ISO 32000-2 §14.9.2.3: "A language identifier attached to a marked-content sequence with the Span tag specifies the language for all text in the sequence except for nested marked-content that is contained in the structure hierarchy (in which case the structure element's language applies) and except where overridden by language specifications for other nested marked-content." and "The Lang entry in the document catalog dictionary shall specify the default natural language for all text in the document."

source: ISO 32000-2 §14.9.2.1: "This applies to both content within content streams and any text strings, including text strings not included in the structure hierarchy such as, for example, entries in metadata, outline entries and names for optional content groups."

summary: Interpretation::speech, pdf-model's public vocalisation of a page, applies a structure element's /Alt per marked-content sequence and only to sequences the element owns directly. A Figure owning two MCIDs is spoken 'A star A star'; a Figure whose one sequence belongs to a child Span element is spoken as its letters, with no description. ContentStream::accessibility reads /Alt (and /E) from the sequence's own parent element, once per sequence. viewer-core's accessibility tree reads an element's /Alt itself and is not affected; no production caller uses Interpretation::speech today.
source: ISO 32000-2 Table 355, Alt: "An alternative description of the structure element and its children in human-readable form". §14.9.3: "When applied to structure elements, the alternate description text (see 7.9.2.2, "Text string type") is a complete (or whole) word or phrase substitution for the current element."
change: Read /Alt and /E through the same walk up /P that structure::enclosing makes for /ActualText (2038-B12's fix), so one description covers all an element encloses and is spoken once.
